samples.question: The picture is a white measurement sheet carrying two separate horizontal rows of short vertical ticks that never touch each other. One row is drawn in pure black: those six or more black ticks are evenly spaced and form the reference lattice. The other row is drawn in red and holds exactly six red gauge ticks; each red tick stands a little way to the left or to the right of one black lattice tick, and no red tick is exactly aligned with a black one. The red row may be drawn above or below the black row; the colours, not the positions, say which row is which. Every pale grey, blue and green mark elsewhere on the sheet is decoration and carries no information. For each red gauge tick, look at the one black lattice tick whose centre is closest to that red tick's centre; the red tick leans left if its centre is to the left of that black tick's centre, and leans right otherwise. How many of the six red gauge ticks lean left? Answer with a single whole number: 1, 2, 3, or 4.
